title: Block: BFS With a Visited Set
oneLiner: Return every node's distance in edges from a start node, using a queue and marking nodes visited when you push them.
keyTakeaway: Mark a node visited when you push it, not when you pop it. Marking on pop lets the same node into the queue several times.
explanation:
adj[i] lists the nodes reachable from node i in one step (edges are directed). Return an array where entry i is the fewest edges from start to node i, or -1 if i can't be reached.

A distance array filled with -1 doubles as the visited set. Set dist[start] = 0 and enqueue start. Pop from the front; for each neighbour still at -1, set its distance to the current node's plus one and enqueue it. Because BFS pops nodes in order of distance, the first time a node is reached is the shortest.

The full lesson is Graphs: Breadth-First Search; this block is the template on its own.

starterCode.python:
def bfs_distances(adj, start):
    # 1. Make a distance array filled with -1; it doubles as the visited set.
    # 2. Set the start's distance to 0 and put it in a queue.
    # 3. While the queue is not empty, take the node at the front.
    # 4. For each neighbour still at -1, set its distance to the node's plus 1 and enqueue it (mark when you push).
    # 5. Return the distances.
    return [0] * len(adj)

gotchas: Marking visited when popping instead of when pushing, so a node can be queued several times.
Using a Python list with pop(0) as the queue: use collections.deque.

complexity.note: Every node is enqueued at most once and every edge is looked at once; the distance array and queue hold up to V nodes.
